choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

(A) secure — (B) migrate — (C) accelerated
(A) hazardous — (B) migrate — (C) restrained
(A) hazardous — (B) produce offspring — (C) accelerated
(A) secure — (B) produce offspring — (C) restrained
choice.ex: (A) hazardous (B) produce offspring (C) restrained 근거 ❷❼❽ 해설: (A) ❷ 초기의 허들이 매우 높았다 = 초기 단계가 가장 위험 / (B) ❼ 번식할 만큼 오래 살지 못함 = 자손을 낳기 전 사망 / (C) ❽ 그렇지 않았다면 인 구 증가가 훨씬 일찍 일어났을 것 = 그동안 증가가 억제됨. accelerated는 ❽과 정반대, migrate는 본문에 없는 내용. 요약문 해석: 아주 최근까지 인간 삶의 가장 초기 단계는 다른 영장류에게 그런 것처럼 통과하기 가장 (A) 위험한 시기였다. 너무 많은 사람이 (B) 자손을 낳기 전에 죽었기 때문에, 역사의 대부분 동안 인구 증가는 (C) 억제된 상태로 남아 있었다.

choice.body: Until quite recently, the earliest stages of human life were the most (A)________ to get through, much as they are for other primates. Because so many died before they could (B)________, population growth remained (C)________ for most of history.

choice.psg: ❶ You might think of survival as a race in which a hurdle has to be jumped every year. ❷ The early hurdles were once very high, and many people fell before clearing the first few. ❸ Demographically, humankind was living close to a state of nature, and nature is extremely wasteful of life. ❹ From only a very small number of figs will even one of many seeds become a fig tree. ❺ Almost a quarter of baboons born in the wild die before they are a year old, which is fairly typical for primates. ❻ Infant mortality rates for humans in pre-modern agricultural societies were similar to, and sometimes higher than, those of apes. ❼ Things were little better for our hunter-gatherer ancestors, a quarter of whom failed to reach their first birthday, while another quarter didn’t live long enough to reproduce just about everywhere until the nineteenth century. ❽ Had it been otherwise, the huge recent growth in human population would have occurred much earlier.
choice.body: In the past, humans suffered the same (A)________ loss of young life that is seen throughout nature, with death rates among babies (B)________ those of apes. Had surviving the first years been far more (C)________, the recent surge in human numbers would have arrived much sooner.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.
opt: The rapid rise in human numbers in recent times is tied to more people surviving their earliest years.
The shift to farming was what first allowed human populations to expand at a rapid pace.
Living in a farming society did not necessarily give babies better chances of survival than baby apes had.
High death rates among the very young are not unique to humans but are shared by other primates.
Getting through the first few years of life was historically one of the greatest challenges humans faced.
choice.ex: ❻ 농업 사회에서도 유아 사망률이 유인원과 비슷하거나 더 높았고, ❼❽ 인구 급증은 19세기 이후 ‘최근’의 일이다. 농경이 빠른 인구 증가를 처음 가능하게 했다는 내용은 본문 근거가 없을 뿐 아니라 ❻❽과 어긋난다(‘농업 = 인구 증가’라는 상식을 이용한 함정). ① 근거 ❼❽ — 최근 인구의 급격한 증가는 더 많은 사람이 생애 초기를 살아남게 된 것과 관련이 있다. ② 근거 없음(정답) — 농경으로의 전환이 처음으로 인구가 빠른 속도로 늘어날 수 있게 한 것이었다. ③ 근거 ❻ — 농업 사회에 산다고 해서 아기들이 새끼 유인원보다 반드시 더 나은 생존 가능성을 가진 것은 아니었다. ④ 근거 ❺❻ — 아주 어린 개체들의 높은 사망률은 인간에게만 있는 것이 아니라 다른 영장류도 공유한다. ⑤ 근거 ❷❻❼ — 생애 첫 몇 해를 넘기는 것은 역사적으로 인간이 직면한 가장 큰 난관 중 하나였다.
choice.psg: ❶ You might think of survival as a race in which a hurdle has to be jumped every year. ❷ The early hurdles were once very high, and many people fell before clearing the first few. ❸ Demographically, humankind was living close to a state of nature, and nature is extremely wasteful of life. ❹ From only a very small number of figs will even one of many seeds become a fig tree. ❺ Almost a quarter of baboons born in the wild die before they are a year old, which is fairly typical for primates. ❻ Infant mortality rates for humans in pre-modern agricultural societies were similar to, and sometimes higher than, those of apes. ❼ Things were little better for our hunter-gatherer ancestors, a quarter of whom failed to reach their first birthday, while another quarter didn’t live long enough to reproduce just about everywhere until the nineteenth century. ❽ Had it been otherwise, the huge recent growth in human population would have occurred much earlier.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: many people struggled with the first obstacles they met when they entered adulthood
people who survived childhood seldom managed to reach old age
early humans were too weak to compete with other species for food
most people stopped competing once they realized how hard the race of life was
a large share of people died before getting through the earliest years of their lives
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 많은 사람들이 처음 몇 개(의 허들)를 넘기 전에 넘어졌다 → 많은 사람이 생애 첫 몇 해를 넘기지 못하고 죽었다 해설: 생존을 ‘매년 허들을 넘는 경주’에 비유했으므로 ‘처음 몇 개의 허들’ = 생애 첫 몇 해, ‘넘어지다(fell)’ = 죽다. 뒤의 ❸~❼(자연의 생명 낭비, 개코원숭 이·인간의 유아 사망률)이 그 의미를 확인해 준다. ‘경쟁을 그만두었다’는 경주의 문자적 의미, ‘성인이 되어 처음 맞닥뜨린 장애물’은 ‘처음’을 성인기의 처 음으로 오독, ‘어린 시절을 살아남은 사람은 노년에 이르기 어려웠다’는 초기가 아닌 후반부 허들로 바꾼 함정, ‘먹이 경쟁’은 무관. ① 많은 사람들이 성인이 되었을 때 처음 맞닥뜨린 장애물들로 고생했다 ② 어린 시절을 살아남은 사람들은 노년에 이르는 경우가 드물었다 ③ 초기 인류는 너무 약해서 다른 종과 먹이를 두고 경쟁할 수 없었다 ④ 대부분의 사람들은 삶이라는 경주가 얼마나 힘든지 깨닫자 경쟁을 그만두었다 ⑤ 많은 비율의 사람들이 생애 가장 초기의 몇 해를 넘기기 전에 죽었다
choice.body: You might think of survival as a race in which a hurdle has to be jumped every year. The early hurdles were once very high, and many people fell before clearing the first few. Demographically, humankind was living close to a state of nature, and nature is extremely wasteful of life.
choice.ul: many people fell before clearing the first few.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) marked — (B) coincide — (C) fall flat
(A) marked — (B) clash — (C) pay off
(A) marked — (B) clash — (C) fall flat
(A) subtle — (B) coincide — (C) pay off
(A) subtle — (B) clash — (C) fall flat
choice.ex: (A) marked (B) clash (C) fall flat 근거 ❶❷❸ 해설: (A) ❷ especial y pronounced = 가장 뚜렷한 / (B) ❷ conflicting messages(내용이 다름) = 충돌하다 / (C) ❸ likely to fail = 효과를 거두지 못 하다(fall flat). coincide(일치하다)는 ❷와 정반대, pay off(성과를 거두다)는 ❸과 정반대. 요약문 해석: 연구에 따르면 사람들은 말보다 비언어적 신호에 더 큰 비중을 두며, 이 경향은 두 종류의 메시지가 (B) 충돌할 때 가장 (A) 뚜렷해진다. 따라 서 몸짓 언어가 다른 이야기를 할 경우, 말만으로 누군가를 이끌려는 시도는 (C) 효과를 거두지 못하는 경향이 있다.
choice.psg: ❶ A study by Eva McMahan, professor of speech communication, confirmed the dominance of nonverbal signals. ❷ The phenomenon, however, was especially pronounced when adults found themselves in situations with conflicting messages (i.e., situations in which the contents of the verbal and nonverbal messages differ). ❸ Attempts to manipulate another person verbally are therefore likely to fail if the accompanying nonverbal communication does not match the spoken message. ❹ This is because people trust nonverbal messages more than verbal ones. ❺ When somebody tells you that they enjoy spending time with you, but you notice how they are looking away and are forcing a smile, you are probably less inclined to believe their words. ❻ The same is probably true when you are back at the office after a sickness and your colleague tells you with a grumpy expression that they were happy to take over your workload. ❼ You might not believe that they enjoyed replacing you while you were gone.
choice.body: Research shows that people give more weight to nonverbal signals than to words, and this tendency becomes most (A)________ when the two kinds of messages (B)________. Consequently, trying to steer someone with words alone tends to (C)________ if one’s body language tells a different story.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

(A) discount — (B) reveals — (C) annoyed

choice.ex: (A) discount (B) reveals (C) annoyed 근거 ❹❺❻ 해설: (A) ❹❺ 비언어적 메시지를 더 믿고 말은 덜 믿음 = discount(곧이듣지 않다) / (B) 표정이 ‘드러내는’ 감정을 믿음 / (C) ❻ grumpy expression = 짜증 난. delighted는 말(happy)과 표정이 일치하는 경우라 설득 실패의 이유가 되지 못함. 요약문 해석: 어떤 사람의 말과 표정이 맞지 않을 때, 듣는 사람들은 그 말을 (A) 깎아서 듣고 얼굴이 (B) 드러내는 것을 믿는 경향이 있다. 따라서 여러분의 일을 떠맡는 것에 대해 쾌활하게 말하지만 (C) 짜증 나 보이는 동료는 아마 여러분을 납득시키지 못할 것이다.
choice.psg: ❶ A study by Eva McMahan, professor of speech communication, confirmed the dominance of nonverbal signals. ❷ The phenomenon, however, was especially pronounced when adults found themselves in situations with conflicting messages (i.e., situations in which the contents of the verbal and nonverbal messages differ). ❸ Attempts to manipulate another person verbally are therefore likely to fail if the accompanying nonverbal communication does not match the spoken message. ❹ This is because people trust nonverbal messages more than verbal ones. ❺ When somebody tells you that they enjoy spending time with you, but you notice how they are looking away and are forcing a smile, you are probably less inclined to believe their words. ❻ The same is probably true when you are back at the office after a sickness and your colleague tells you with a grumpy expression that they were happy to take over your workload. ❼ You might not believe that they enjoyed replacing you while you were gone.
choice.body: When a person’s words and expressions do not line up, listeners tend to (A)________ the words and believe what the face (B)________. Thus, a coworker who sounds cheerful about taking on your tasks but looks (C)________ will probably not convince you.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.
opt: Nonverbal signals were shown to carry little weight whenever spoken and unspoken messages agreed.
Adults rely even more heavily on unspoken cues when verbal and nonverbal signals conflict.
A person’s facial expression can make listeners doubt what that person is actually saying.
Nonverbal cues can undermine the credibility of a spoken message when the two point in different directions.
Someone hoping to persuade others should make sure that their gestures fit what they say.
choice.ex: ❶ 연구는 비언어적 신호의 우위를 (일반적으로) 확인했고, ❷ 모순 상황에서 ‘특히’ 두드러졌을 뿐이다. ‘특히’를 ‘그때만’으로 확대해 일치하는 상황에서는 비언어적 신호가 거의 중요하지 않다고 보는 것은 본문에서 추론할 수 없다(❶과도 어긋남). ① 근거 없음(정답) — 말과 비언어적 메시지가 일치할 때마다 비언어적 신호는 거의 중요하지 않은 것으로 나타났다. ② 근거 ❷ — 성인들은 언어적 신호와 비언어적 신호가 충돌할 때 말해지지 않은 신호에 훨씬 더 크게 의존한다. ③ 근거 ❺❻❼ — 한 사람의 얼굴 표정은 듣는 사람이 그 사람이 실제로 하는 말을 의심하게 만들 수 있다. ④ 근거 ❷❸❹ — 비언어적 신호는 말과 서로 다른 방향을 가리킬 때 말로 된 메시지의 신뢰성을 떨어뜨릴 수 있다. ⑤ 근거 ❸ — 다른 사람을 설득하려는 사람은 자신의 몸짓이 말과 맞는지 확인해야 한다.
choice.psg: ❶ A study by Eva McMahan, professor of speech communication, confirmed the dominance of nonverbal signals. ❷ The phenomenon, however, was especially pronounced when adults found themselves in situations with conflicting messages (i.e., situations in which the contents of the verbal and nonverbal messages differ). ❸ Attempts to manipulate another person verbally are therefore likely to fail if the accompanying nonverbal communication does not match the spoken message. ❹ This is because people trust nonverbal messages more than verbal ones. ❺ When somebody tells you that they enjoy spending time with you, but you notice how they are looking away and are forcing a smile, you are probably less inclined to believe their words. ❻ The same is probably true when you are back at the office after a sickness and your colleague tells you with a grumpy expression that they were happy to take over your workload. ❼ You might not believe that they enjoyed replacing you while you were gone.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: the colleague hides negative feelings so well that no one could notice them
the colleague’s cheerful words are contradicted by a face that shows displeasure
the colleague worries that you are still too sick to come back to work
the colleague is sincerely pleased to have handled the extra work
the colleague openly complains in words about the heavy workload
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 여러분의 동료가 언짢은 표정으로 여러분의 업무를 떠맡게 되어 즐거웠다고 말한다 → 말(즐거움)과 표정(불쾌)이 모순된다 해설: ‘즐거웠다(happy)’는 말과 ‘언짢은 표정(grumpy expression)’이 동시에 전달되는 상황 = ❷의 모순되는 메시지. 이어지는 ❼ “여러분은 그 말을 믿 지 않을 것이다”가 이를 확인. ‘진심으로 기뻐한다’는 말만 믿은 해석, ‘감정을 너무 잘 숨긴다’는 표정이 감정을 드러낸다는 점과 반대, ‘말로 대놓고 불평한 다’는 불만의 전달 통로를 바꾼 함정, ‘아직 아플까 걱정한다’는 무관. ① 동료는 부정적인 감정을 너무 잘 숨겨서 아무도 알아챌 수 없다 ② 동료의 쾌활한 말이 불쾌감을 보여 주는 얼굴과 모순된다 ③ 동료는 여러분이 아직 너무 아파서 복귀할 수 없을까 봐 걱정한다 ④ 동료는 추가 업무를 처리한 것에 진심으로 기뻐한다 ⑤ 동료는 과중한 업무에 대해 말로 대놓고 불평한다
choice.body: When somebody tells you that they enjoy spending time with you, but you notice how they are looking away and are forcing a smile, you are probably less inclined to believe their words. The same is probably true when you are back at the office after a sickness and your colleague tells you with a grumpy expression that they were happy to take over your workload. You might not believe that they enjoyed replacing you while you were gone.
choice.ul: your colleague tells you with a grumpy expression that they were happy to take over your workload.

howto.word: 단락마다 밑줄 친 (번호) 중 어법·어휘상 틀린 것을 찾아요. 밑줄이 하나씩 나오면 O(맞음) 또는 X(틀림)를 누르고, X는 바로 아래 칸에 고쳐 씁니다. 어휘는 원문과 단어가 달라도 뜻이 같으면 O, 글의 흐름과 반대면 X예요. 틀린 부분만 써도 되고 밑줄 전체나 문장 전체로 고쳐 써도 됩니다(정답이 들어 있으면 정답). 밑줄을 모두 O·X 해야 다음 단락으로 넘어가요.
